title: JPEG baseline encoder (T.81) for NV12 + 'jpeg' VideoToolbox encoder object
state: implemented and host-tested; the plug-in objects compile for arm64-apple-ios16.0; nothing was run on the phone

commands.components: 162 unit checks under ASan+UBSan + the same 162 under plain -O2 + 77 oracle checks
172 checks under ASan+UBSan + 172 under TSan + one arm64-apple-ios16.0 compile with -Werror

commands.last_line: ld64.lld: error: undefined symbol: __tlv_bootstrap (and _pthread_* / _fprintf from avc/, kern/)
commands.note: Posted to the board with owners. R1 objects were compiled separately for iOS and every import checked against sdk/lib/*.tbd.

done: T.81 baseline JPEG encoder in jpeg/n2jpeg.c, driven only through the public jpeg/n2jpeg.h API
4:2:0 taken directly from NV12 (luma 2x2, Cb/Cr 1x1 sampling factors); no colour conversion, no chroma resampling
every 8x8 block's level shift + forward DCT + quantisation done by n2vk_fdct8_quant(); edge blocks are gathered with edge replication and the block buffer is always stride 8
Annex K.1-K.6 tables written out literally; canonical Huffman codes built at open with over-subscription and all-ones-code rejection
IJG quality scaling of the Annex K quantisation tables with the baseline clamp 1..255; quality 50 is the identity and is tested against the literal tables
DQT stored in zigzag order; coefficients coded in zigzag order; DC differential with per-component predictors reset at restarts
DRI + RSTn restart markers at the exact MCU boundaries, 1-bit padding before each marker and before EOI, RSTn cycling 0..7
0xFF stuffing in the entropy-coded data; restart markers are not stuffed
APPn (0xE0..0xEF) and COM (0xFE) segments passed in by the caller, copied at open; a caller APP0 suppresses the JFIF APP0
odd dimensions rejected (NV12 needs even); 2..65534 supported; non-MCU-multiple sizes tested at 2x2, 18x18, 34x20, 178x146

buffer contract: n2jpeg_encode(enc, pic, NULL, 0, &size) gives the exact size; a short buffer returns N2JPEG_E_TOO_SMALL with the exact size and writes nothing past the capacity; no allocation in the per-picture path
n2jpeg_bound() = header + MCUs * (6 * 416 + 4), a guaranteed upper bound including worst-case stuffing

VideoToolbox glue vt/n2jpeg_vt.c: CMBaseObject/VTVideoEncoder vtable per n2vt_abi.h, one CMSampleBuffer per frame, 'jpeg' CMVideoFormatDescription, sync-sample attachments, one emit per submitted frame including error paths, finalize frees everything
26 standard properties accepted and stored; Quality (0..1) maps to the JPEG quality 1..100; UsingHardwareAcceleratedVideoEncoder=false; NumberOfPendingFrames=0

iOS: jpeg/n2jpeg.c, vt/n2jpeg_vt.c, kern/n2vk_ref.c compile for arm64-apple-ios16.0 with PLAN 4.3 flags and zero warnings; all their imports are covered by sdk/lib/*.tbd except __tlv_bootstrap (kern/n2vk_dispatch.c, WP08)
segment payload ownership: n2jpeg_open() copies APPn/COM payloads, so the caller may free them immediately (tested by freeing the payload before the encode)
not_done: Nothing has run on the phone. The encoder has never seen a real CVPixelBuffer from mediaserverd; the glue has only run against WP02's fake runtime.

CMVideoFormatDescriptionCreate() has never executed: WP02's fake does not implement it, so the host test exercises the NULL-format-description branch. The glue takes the real branch as soon as the fake has the symbol; on the phone the symbol is a weak import and its presence was not verified here (the lead checks the cache).
Repeated StartSession on one live encoder object is not host-tested: the fake has no accessor for its session handle, so a second startSession cannot be driven without a made-up pointer.

The full plug-in link for iOS is currently blocked by symbols from other packages (_pthread_create/join/cond_* and _fprintf from avc/, __tlv_bootstrap from kern/n2vk_dispatch.c). Reported on the board with owners; not R1 files.
No integration with install/ or the probe: whether VideoToolbox's 'jpeg' encoder registry entry is what CMPhoto accepts is untested; the stage-0/CMPhoto question stays with the lead's phone cycles.
Baseline only by design: no progressive JPEG, no 16-bit quantisation tables (SOF1), no optimised Huffman tables, no 4:4:4/4:2:2 or RGB input, no EXIF generation (pass-through only).
Single-threaded encoder; TSan covers two independent encoder objects on two threads, not one object shared by threads (the glue serialises one object with a mutex).
Performance is host-only: 1280x720 at quality 90 took 19-21 ms on this machine (one core, -O2). No phone measurement.
known_risks: CMPhoto may insist on a hardware-accelerated JPEG encoder (kCMPhotoCompressionOption_RequireHardwareCodec was found on one path). The glue reports hardware=false; nord2-video-claim-hw is the only lever and may have side effects.

A 'jpeg' CMVideoFormatDescription carries no codec-specific extensions. Clients that expect a still-image container description (rather than a video format description with codecType 'jpeg') may refuse the sample buffer; this is not provable without the phone.
The glue grows its output buffer once with realloc if a picture needs more than width*height/2 + 64 KiB (rare; quality-100 noise at very large sizes). After the first grow the buffer is stable.
n2jpeg_bound() is conservative (up to ~92 MB for 4096x2304); callers that allocate it blindly should prefer the exact size from the NULL-buffer call.

The quality scale is IJG's, not T.81's: at quality < 25 the tables saturate at 255 exactly like 'cjpeg -baseline', while default cjpeg switches to 16-bit tables and SOF1 (non-baseline). This is a deliberate baseline-only choice.
The VT glue accepts only 420v/420f and rejects i420 with an error emit; a client that only produces i420 would get no frames.
The VT glue caps still dimensions at 8192x8192 (32 MiB initial buffer); a larger request is refused at startSession with kVTParameterErr. The encoder API itself accepts up to 65534.
